"Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?" (105:1)

This interrogative form is adopted to express wonder: this was a remarkable event, it contains a great lesson, and great meanings are hidden within it. This event was well known among the Arabs. Indeed, the Arabs began their calendar from this event, and it became an important date in their history. People would say, "such-and-such event happened in the year of the Elephant," "such-and-such event happened two years before the Year of the Elephant," and "such-and-such event happened ten years after the Year of the Elephant." And the well-known narration is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was also born in the Year of the Elephant, which was a remarkable coincidence in accordance with the decrees of destiny.

In short, this surah did not narrate any event that they did not know. It was an event that was within their knowledge, and the Qur'an reminded them of it. And the purpose was to draw their attention to what follows.

After this, the next clause is also interrogative, but the question is rhetorical, that is, a question whose answer is affirmative.

﴿Did He not make their plan go astray?﴾ (2:105). That is, He did not let their scheming and planning reach its target and arrive at its goal, by making it go astray in the same way that a person loses his way and is unable to reach the destination he intended. In this manner, Allah reminds the Quraysh that He bestowed favour and kindness upon them, supported them, and saved this House at a time when they themselves were unable to face the mighty army of Abrahah. Perhaps they would feel shame and not deny that Being who gave them help in a state of great weakness and helplessness. Their condition at that time was exactly like that of Abrahah. They wanted to trample the handful of Muslims of Makkah under their pride and power. They should remember well the mighty one who marched against the House of Allah and intended to violate its sanctity. Allah has the power that, just as He saved the House of Allah, He can likewise save the Party of Allah (ḥizb Allāh) that carries His call.

The question is: how then did Allah make their cunning go astray and bring it to nothing? The Qur'an, in a very beautiful manner, also portrays this scene.

﴿And He sent against them flocks of birds, which pelted them with stones of baked clay, and He made them like straw eaten up.﴾ (105:3-5)

Ababil (105:3) means flocks.

Sijjil (105:4) is a Persian loanword that has been Arabicised (ma'rab), and is made up of two words, "sang" and "gil," meaning clay stone. It means that the clay was baked and turned into stones, or that these were stones mixed with mud.

Ka'asf (105:5) means dried leaves of trees. The description of ka'asf as "eaten" (ma'kul) means that it has been eaten, that is, the state of the leaves is that they have been eaten and ground up by creeping creatures, or chewed and reduced to fine pieces by animals. This is a sensory depiction, from which it is understood that when the flocks of birds struck them with stones, their bodies were reduced to pieces. Therefore there is no need for such interpretations as that their bodies were reduced to pieces because of smallpox or measles.

The facts stated in this event are instructive and enlightening for us from several angles:

First, it appears that Allah did not wish that the protection and defence of His House be carried out through the polytheists. Although they attributed themselves to this House, tried to protect it, and sought refuge in it, when Allah intended to protect this House, to safeguard it, to declare His support for it, and to show His jealousy over it, He made the condition of the polytheists of Makkah such that they were helpless before that aggressive force, and the power of God became fully manifest in protecting His House, which is a sacred house, so that the polytheists would have no historical role in the protection of the Sacred House, which is governed by the pretence of the zeal of ignorance (hamiyyat al-jahiliyyah). This point also gives preference to the view that Allah adopted an extraordinary and miraculous manner in the destruction of that invading army, and that no ordinary, customary method was used for their destruction. This is the more appropriate and more probable view.

The requirement of this open intervention in defence of the Ka'bah was that the Quraysh and the Arabs spread around the Sacred House should, after the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ), themselves have entered Islam, and should not have boasted of their service to and pre-eminence over the Sacred House; and the network of idol worship they had spread around the Sacred House should not have been an obstacle to their entry into Islam. But regrettably they did not accept Islam. For this reason, in this Surah the incident has been mentioned in such a manner as to shame the people of Quraysh, and this is in effect a criticism of them and an expression of wonder at their hostile stance, why they did not take a lesson from this event.

Secondly, it appears that Allah did not grant the People of the Book, Abrahah and his army, the ability to demolish this House and to establish their rule over this sacred land, even though the custodians of this House were polytheists, so that this House would remain free from the domination of any imperialist power, so that no foreign conspiracy would operate in this region, and so that the freedom of this land would be preserved, so that the new religion and the new ideology that, by the decree of Allah, was destined to arise from here, would emerge in an atmosphere of freedom, not be under the pressure of any governmental authority, and so that no foreign dictator could rebel here, and no religion would be superior to this religion, which was to encompass all religions and which was to take in hand the task of guiding all humanity, while it was itself in need of no one's guidance. This was the plan of Allah for the Last Prophet and his religion. This was taking place at a time when people did not know that the leader of this new religion had been born that very year.

Today, the global crusaders and global Zionism look upon the sacred places of the Muslims with shameless and greedy eyes, and we know well their deceitful plans. But the indications we receive from this Surah give us a measure of tranquillity, that no conspiracy of theirs against the sacred places of Islam can succeed. The Allah who protected His House from the People of the Book at a time when its custodians and attendants were polytheists will certainly protect it today. Likewise, Allah will protect the city of His Prophet from these conspiracies and covetous, deceitful eyes.

Thirdly, in the past, the Arabs had no noteworthy role on this earth; rather, before Islam they had no real existence. In Yemen they were slaves of the Persians and the Abyssinians. If any government of the Arabs was established in southern Arabia, it was under the mandate of the Iranians. In the north, the region of Syria was under the Roman empire. This region was either directly under the Roman empire, or they established under their protection some Arab kingdom here. Only the heart of the Arabian Peninsula was an area free from the influence of any foreign government, but this region had no global role. It was a backward, Bedouin region. When tribal war broke out in this area, it would continue for forty years at a stretch. Because of this disorder, the inhabitants of these regions had no value in the eyes of neighbouring countries. Their military status became evident during the campaign of the People of the Elephant (Ashab al-Fil), that they had no capacity to confront any foreign invader.

The opportunity to play a global role for the Arabs was first granted under the banner of Islam. A global state came into being for them, which had a status, and which people also counted. This was in effect a global revolution, like a flood. In this revolution many states were swept away, many thrones collapsed, and the leadership of humanity came to the Arabs. This happened at the time when the authority of misguided and corrupt leaderships on this earth was stripped away. The real question is: when and why did the Arabs attain this position? They attained this position at the time when they forgot that they were Arabs. They forgot the slogans of regional, racial and linguistic asabiyyah (tribal and national solidarity). They remembered only that they were Muslims, and only Muslims. They raised only the banners of Islam, and they rose up carrying a great ideology of life and delivered it to all people. They became a source of mercy for humanity and of good for it. They raised neither the slogan of nationalism nor that of racial asabiyyah, but rather they rose up bearing a thought based on heavenly guidance, and presented it to people as heavenly guidance. They did not take the religion of Islam as a worldly religion and worldly ideology, with the aim that they would establish some Arab imperialism, so that under its shade they could roam and graze freely on this earth, so that their noses would be raised high, and so that they would become great in the world through that empire, and draw people out of the rule of the Romans and Persians into the rule of the Arabs. Rather, they rose up so that they could bring people out of the servitude of human beings and into the worship of Allah alone. As Rib'i ibn 'Amir, the representative of the Muslims, said in the court of Yazdgerd: "Allah has raised us so that we may bring people out of the servitude of human beings into the servitude of Allah, and from the narrowness of this world into the vastness of the Hereafter, and bring the common people out of the oppression of other religions into the justice of Islam."

This was the time when the existence of the Arabs was established in the world, when they gained strength, and when their leadership was founded. But this call was for Allah and this struggle was in the way of Allah. This power remained in place for a period; for a time they were the leaders of humanity, as long as they remained upon their way. When they deviated from the Islamic ideology of life, and became proponents of tribal asabiyyah, and instead of raising the banners of Allah they took up the banners of asabiyyah, then the earth threw them off, and the nations of the world trampled them underfoot, because they abandoned Allah, so Allah abandoned them, and just as they forgot Allah, Allah also forgot them.

The question is: apart from Islam, what is the status of the Arabs? If they set aside Islamic belief, Islamic concepts and thoughts, what do they have that they can present to humanity? And if a nation has no message for humanity, what is such a nation worth? The history of the world bears witness that those nations which at any time led humanity had a thought, had a message which they gave to humanity. Those nations which had no message, such as the Tatars, who trampled the whole East and who also destroyed the Roman empire in the Arab world, did not survive for a long time, but dissolved into the very nations they had conquered. Remember that the ideology with which the Arabs endowed humanity was solely the Islamic ideology of life. Because of this ideology they attained the position of global leadership. When they cast this ideology behind them, then they had no work left on this earth; their role in history came to an end. Today, if the Arabs wish to live, they should keep this lesson in mind. If they want strength and leadership, otherwise no status can be established for them. It is Allah alone who can guide the misguided.
